1.title: A book from an Egyptian scroll
1.text: The Book of Abraham is part of the Pearl of Great Price. Latter-day Saints hold it as Abraham's own record, written in the first person — notice how chapter 1 opens with 'I, Abraham.'

1.question: In Abraham 1:1, what did Abraham find he needed to obtain?
options: Another place of residence
A new priest for his household
A large army of his own
A ship for the journey

1.question: In Abraham 1:5, why did Abraham's fathers refuse to hearken to his voice?
options: They had turned to worshiping the gods of the heathen
Because they obeyed the orders of the priest of Elkenah
Because they believed that Abraham lied about his own visions
Because they wished to keep their alliance with Pharaoh

1.template: they would not bow down to worship gods of {0} or of stone

1.question: According to Abraham 1:15-16, who delivered Abraham as the priest lifted his hands to slay him?
options: An angel sent from heaven, who bound the priest
The Lord, who declared his name is Jehovah
His father Terah, who suddenly repented
The king of Egypt, who claimed the sacrifice

1.question: In Abraham 1:19, the Lord says that as it was with whom, so shall it be with Abraham?
options: Adam
Enoch
Noah
Moses

1.question: In Abraham 1:21-24, from whose loins was the king of Egypt descended?
options: Shem
Japheth
Ham
Melchizedek

1.question: According to Abraham 1:28-30, what did the Lord preserve in Abraham's own hands?
options: The treasures and many flocks that his father Terah gathered in Ur
The records of the fathers concerning the right of Priesthood
The images of the gods carved by the priests of Pharaoh
The knowledge of astronomy taught to the Egyptians

2.question: In Abraham 2:3-4, to what land did the Lord command Abraham to go?
options: The land of Egypt, his father's home
A land the Lord would show him
The city of Babylon, full of idols
The kingdom of Assyria, at war

2.template: I will {0} them that bless thee, and curse them that curse thee

2.title: Sixty-two years old
2.text: Abraham 2:14 gives a rare, specific detail: Abraham was 'sixty and two years old' when he departed out of Haran — a reminder that this is written as a personal, remembered record.

2.question: In Abraham 2:15-16, whom did Abraham take with him as he journeyed toward Canaan?
options: Only his servants
Sarai his wife and Lot
Pharaoh's daughter
The priest of Elkenah

2.question: In Abraham 2:22-23, what did the Lord warn about Sarai as they neared Egypt?
options: That Sarai would be taken as a servant in Pharaoh's house
The Egyptians would see she was fair and kill Abraham
That Sarai would fall gravely ill because of the desert journey
That the Egyptians would rejoice and give them riches

3.question: In Abraham 3:2-3, what is the name of the great star nearest to the throne of God?
options: Shinehah
Kokob
Kolob
Olea

3.title: A day is a thousand years
3.text: Abraham 3:4 says one revolution of Kolob is 'a day unto the Lord,' being 'one thousand years' by earthly reckoning — an idea echoed in 2 Peter 3:8.

3.question: In Abraham 3:9, one comes near the throne of God as one comes near what?
options: The sun
Kolob
The moon
The earth

3.question: According to Abraham 3:18, what is said of the two spirits — that they are 'gnolaum'?
options: They were created together in that very same instant
They are eternal, having no beginning and no end
They will end when the earth is destroyed
They are unequal because one has no body

3.question: In Abraham 3:22-23, the Lord tells Abraham he was among the noble and great ones and was chosen when?
options: After he was born
Before he was born
When he entered Egypt
When he received the Priesthood

3.question: In Abraham 3:27, who answers 'Here am I, send me' and is chosen — the Lord says 'I will send the first'?
options: The one like unto the Son of Man
The eldest among the spirits there
The angel set at God's right hand
The one who refused to be sent

4.title: The Gods organized
4.text: Unlike Genesis, Abraham 4 says the Gods 'organized and formed' the heavens and the earth — organizing existing materials rather than creating from nothing.

4.question: In Abraham 4:5, what did the Gods call the light and the darkness?
options: Morning and Evening
Day and Night
Sun and Moon
Good and Evil

4.template: And the Gods called the expanse, {0}

4.question: According to Abraham 4:14, what did the Gods organize the lights in the expanse to be for?
options: To warm and give light to the earth
Signs, seasons, days, and years
To separate the nations and peoples
To guide the angels upon their paths

4.question: In Abraham 4:16, which of the two great lights was set to rule the day?
options: The lesser light
The greater light
The stars
Kolob

4.question: In Abraham 4:24-25, on which 'time' did the Gods prepare the earth to bring forth cattle and beasts?
options: The third time
The fifth time
The sixth time
The seventh time

4.question: According to Abraham 4:27, the Gods formed man in whose image?
options: In the image of the angels who served them
In the image of the Gods, male and female
In the image of the first spirit created
In the likeness of the animals they would rule

5.question: In Abraham 5:2-3, on which 'time' did the Gods rest from all their work?
options: The fifth time
The sixth time
The seventh time
The first time

5.title: Time reckoned by Kolob
5.text: Abraham 5:13 pauses to note that this was 'after the Lord's time, which was after the time of Kolob' — tying the creation account back to the astronomy of chapter 3.

5.question: In Abraham 5:11-13, what did the Gods command about the tree of knowledge of good and evil?
options: That only the woman should eat
That he should guard it with fire
That man should not eat of it
That beasts must never touch it

5.question: In Abraham 5:14-17, why did the Gods form a help meet for the man?
options: Because it was not good that the man should be alone
Because the man had earnestly asked God for a companion
Because none of the animals could obey or serve him
Because the garden still needed one more guardian
